architecture.overview: Azure Functions v2 app (Python) deployed to a Consumption plan. Each HTTP trigger handles one REST operation. Content is organized into named sections, each with its own schema and visibility rules. Both current sections — writing and diary — use HistoryApiStorage exclusively: every get/list/create/update/delete call is an HTTP request to [[history-api]], which is now the sole storage backend, not an optional add-on. Auth uses google-auth to validate Google ID tokens server-side; no session state is maintained. Private sections enforce authentication and ownership checks for all operations, including reads. Application Insights is integrated for backend telemetry, automatically capturing HTTP request metrics (e.g., route, method, status, duration, exceptions) for all endpoints.

Content is organized into named sections, each with its own schema and visibility rules. Both current sections — writing and diary — use HistoryApiStorage exclusively: every get/list/create/update/delete call is an HTTP request to [[history-api|history-api]], which is now the sole storage backend, not an optional add-on. The repo also still contains GitHub- and Blob-Storage-backed storage classes from before the history-api migration; neither is wired into any current section and both are exercised only by their own unit tests. summary: Azure Functions (Python) API that manages private content sections — currently writing and diary, both fully backed by [[history-api]]. Authentication is handled via Google ID tokens; content ownership is enforced per-creator, with an allowlist controlling who can write. Application Insights provides backend telemetry for HTTP request metrics.
